verified_behaviors: The supervised command starts in its own session and process group; cleanup targets only that task group.
Stop, timeout and leader exit clean and reap CPU fixture descendants that ignore SIGTERM, escalating to SIGKILL within the owned group when necessary.
A separate sentinel process group remains alive during supervised-group cleanup.
A catchable supervisor signal or an exception after child launch still invokes owned-group cleanup.
Unconfirmed cleanup reports exit code 125 and process_group_terminated=false without a success exit marker.
An unavailable Linux subreaper fails before launch; a missing command is explicitly recorded as command_started=false.
Native Linux MatterGen command construction uses the supervisor; unsupported Windows native construction directs the user to WSL.
limitations: An uncatchable SIGKILL delivered to the supervisor, host shutdown or host failure is outside the cleanup guarantee.
A descendant that deliberately creates a new session or leaves the owned process group is outside the cleanup guarantee. This supervisor is not a security sandbox.
CPU substitute programs validate process lifecycle behavior; they do not establish GPU execution, model output correctness, remote deployment or material properties.
The cleanup-confirmation failure case uses fault injection after real CPU cleanup; it validates the uncertainty report rather than simulating an unkillable operating-system process.
Windows native material execution is unsupported; the Windows run covers command construction and rejection only.
